# E1 — 64² pre-screen of transport-dominated 2D Navier–Stokes families (no training)

**Status: final for the 64² screen; every number is generated by the scripts beside this file
(`table.md` is written by `analyze_e1.py`, the scaling/travel numbers by `extras_e1.py`).**
Directory: `/tmp/claude-1002/-home-tahmid-Dev-pod-ae-nmrom-Tunable-NM-ROM-Claude/6e5fe858-5d6b-4b34-a1bd-df699b1d4032/scratchpad/ns-invest/e1/`.
Nothing was written inside any worktree; no cluster job; three local GPU runs through `jaxrun-slot`
(smoke 16 s, main 197 s, variant 108 s; all `backend gpu`, `x64`, `JAX_DEFAULT_MATMUL_PRECISION=highest`).

## Verdict in one paragraph

None of the four pre-registered candidates (A control, B advected vortex pair, C drifting Kolmogorov,
D thin shear layer) passes both thresholds as first defined. The variant **B2** — the vortex pair with
sharper cores ($\sigma = 0.06$), the narrower Reynolds range $\nu \in [10^{-3}, 3\cdot10^{-3}]$
(Re 330–1000) and **no** background flow (4 parameters: $\Gamma, d, \theta, \nu$) — is the only family
that passes coverage (**0.244 ≤ 0.25**) while sitting on the floor threshold: POD-16 floor
**0.345** on the head report's definition (median over all held-out states; threshold 0.35, missed by
0.005) and **0.386** on the task's definition (worst evolved time per case, median over cases; passes).
Its control arm B3 (same cores and Re range, background flow kept, 6 parameters) shows what each lever
does: the sharper, less-diffused cores raise the floor (0.235 → 0.38), the two dropped background-flow
parameters bring coverage down (0.449 → 0.244). **Recommended family for E2: B2.** Two things E2 must
carry from this screen: (i) B2's nonlinearity is almost entirely the translation — after the head
report's spectral phase alignment its POD-16 floor is **0.082** and its coverage **0.138** — so the
*aligned* linear ROM, not the raw POD-16, is the control a shifted-manifold decoder has to beat; (ii)
no family makes the FOM expensive (Newton 2.00 iterations/step everywhere), so the cost side of the
story is unchanged.

## The two statistics, exactly as computed (`analyze_e1.py`)

Both follow the head report §2.3 / `analyze_b.py` so that family A reproduces its numbers.

- **POD-K floor.** $V_K$ = the first $K$ left singular vectors of the matrix of **all** training states
  (128 trajectories × 26 outputs = 3328 snapshots, mean not subtracted, as in the lane). For each
  held-out case $c$ and output time $t$:
  $e_{c,t} = \|x_{c,t} - V_K V_K^{\top} x_{c,t}\|_2 \,/\, \|\omega_c(0)\|_2$.
  `floor_all` = median of $e_{c,t}$ over the 32 × 6 states (the head report's statistic);
  `floor_worst_evolved` = median over cases of $\max_{t>0} e_{c,t}$ (the wording of the E1 task);
  `floor_t0`, `floor_evolved`, `per_time` are the obvious splits. K ∈ {16, 32, 64}.
- **Same-time coverage.** For each held-out state $x_{c,t}$, the minimum over the 128 training states
  *at the same output index* of $\|u^{\mathrm{tr}} - x_{c,t}\|_2 / \|\omega_c(0)\|_2$; median over the
  32 × 6 states. `any_time_all` drops the same-index restriction.

Reproduction: on the head's own cohort (282 train / 64 dev) this script gives 0.2389 / 0.6441 against
the head report's 0.239 / 0.644; on the E1 128/32 sub-cohort of the same seeds 0.237 / 0.665 (the
coverage rises by the expected $(128/282)^{-1/13} \approx 1.06$).

## Generators — exact definitions, seeds, horizons

FOM: the lane's certified `ns2d_fom.py` (commit of worktree `2026-09-17-ns2d`, imported read-only)
extended in `fom_ext.py` by two terms the lane's mean-zero-$\psi$ gauge cannot express:

$$\omega_t = J_A(\psi,\omega) + \nu\,\Delta_h\omega \;-\; (U\,\omega_x + V\,\omega_y) \;+\; f(x,y,t),
\qquad \Delta_h\psi = -\omega,$$

with centred differences for the uniform advection (skew-symmetric), implicit midpoint, Newton to
$10^{-11}$ relative, BiCGStab to $10^{-9}$ with the exact FFT Helmholtz preconditioner — all the lane's
code paths. With $U=V=0$ and $f=0$ the added terms are exact zeros: the smoke run reproduces the head
investigation's `data64.npz` for family A **bitwise** (`smoke.log`: max rel diff 0.000e+00).
Trajectories are vmapped in chunks of 32 (per-trajectory $\nu$, $(U,V)$, forcing parameters are
jit/vmap arguments, never closure constants). Grid $64^2$, $dt = 2\cdot10^{-3}$, 26 saved states.

Seeds (all families): training = `draw(20260917, 512)[:128]`, held-out = `draw(20260918, 64)[:32]`,
column-by-column draws (the lane's `params_draw` convention, so the sets extend consistently).
$\nu \sim \log U[10^{-3}, 10^{-2}]$ (Re 100–1000 at unit velocity) unless stated.

## What the screen says, family by family

- **A** reproduces the head report and fails both (0.237 / 0.665). **E** (3 modes) is nearly linear
  (0.078) and *still* uncovered (0.497): fewer parameters alone do not buy coverage on a decaying family
  whose states spread through their own dynamics.
- **B** (6 params, Re 100–1000): the floor is only 0.235 because at $\nu = 10^{-2}$ the cores blur
  ($\sqrt{2\nu T} = 0.17 > \sigma$; held-out E(T)/E(0) = 0.46, Z(T)/Z(0) = 0.27) into low modes, and
  the relative errors are divided by $\|\omega(0)\|$ while the norm halves. Coverage 0.363 is already the
  best of the first four. Per-time coverage 0.17 → 0.42: the spread comes from where the dipoles go.
- **C** (drifting Kolmogorov) has the most nonlinear *evolved* states of all (worst-evolved floor
  0.546, POD-64 still 0.16, energy fraction in 16 modes 0.72), but raw coverage jumps from 0.046 at
  $t=0$ to 0.63 at the first output: the $k=4$ stripes (wavelength 0.25) decorrelate under any mismatch
  of drift speed or angle, so a same-time nearest neighbour in the raw $L^2$ metric does not exist at any
  affordable sample count. After alignment its coverage is 0.136 (would pass) and its floor 0.146
  (would fail). C is the family to revisit only if E2's decoder aligns *before* it interpolates.
- **D** (shear layer) is linear at this Re range: with $\delta \le 0.06$ and $\nu \ge 10^{-3}$ the
  layer Reynolds number $\delta/\nu$ is 3–60, the diffusion length over the horizon
  ($\sqrt{2\nu T} = 0.045$–$0.14$) exceeds the layer thickness, and the base layer (peak vorticity
  $1/\delta \approx 17$–33) outweighs the perturbation ($2\pi\varepsilon \lesssim 0.6$) by 30–100× in
  norm. POD energy in 16 modes is 0.999. A Kelvin–Helmholtz family needs $\nu \lesssim 10^{-4}$
  ($Re_\delta \gtrsim 300$), outside the pre-registered Re range and marginal at $64^2$ ($\delta =
  0.03$ is two cells). Not pursued.
- **The variant.** B2 raises the floor to 0.345 / 0.386 and lowers coverage to 0.244; B3 isolates the
  levers (floor 0.377 with the same cores and Re range; coverage 0.449 with the background flow's two
  extra parameters). With training-set size (`extras_e1.json`) the B2 floor is flat (0.351 / 0.354 /
  0.345 at 32 / 64 / 128 trajectories — the basis is saturated) while coverage falls as
  $n_{\rm tr}^{-0.28}$ (0.361 / 0.301 / 0.244), extrapolating to **0.165 at 512** and 0.11 at 2048
  trajectories. At $256^2$ the cores are 15 cells wide instead of 3.8, which can only sharpen the
  translated structure (floor up); the 64² floor of B2 is therefore a lower-side estimate.

### The structural tension the screen exposes

The two thresholds pull against each other for any transport family: a high POD floor needs a
structure that is compact relative to the domain (many Fourier modes per translated state), while
same-time raw-$L^2$ coverage needs the *positions* of that structure to be sampled at a spacing
smaller than its width. With 128 trajectories the vortex pair at $\sigma = 0.06$ is the compromise that
lands on both thresholds at once; anything finer (C's stripes, a KH roll-up) fails coverage by
decorrelation, anything broader (B at $\sigma = 0.08$ with diffusion) fails the floor. That is also
why the aligned statistics of every transport family are far better than the raw ones (B2: 0.082 /
0.138): the difficulty is the translation, and a decoder that removes it exactly meets a nearly linear
residual. For E2 this means the **aligned POD-16 floor (≈ 0.08 at 64²) is the linear control that
matters**; the H-ORACLE bar against raw POD-16 (0.345) is met by the shift alone.

## Recommendation for E2

Run E2 on **B2** ($\sigma = 0.06$, $\Gamma \sim U[0.5,1.5]$, $d \sim U[0.15,0.25]$, $\theta \sim
U[0,2\pi)$, $\nu \sim \log U[10^{-3}, 3\cdot10^{-3}]$, no background flow, $T = 1.5$, seeds 20260917 /
20260918), at $256^2$ with 512 training trajectories (predicted coverage ≈ 0.17, floor ≥ 0.35).
Pre-register three controls beside the raw POD-16: the aligned POD-14/16 (the symmetry-reduced linear
ROM; ≈ 0.08 here), the free-code auto-decoder (must fail, as in the plan), and — because the
background flow is now absent — state explicitly that the family's transport is self-induced, so a
"Galilean-shift" decoder has to *infer* the shift from the state rather than read it from a parameter.
If E2 wants a family whose residual after alignment is itself nonlinear, C is the candidate (aligned
floor 0.146, aligned coverage 0.136) but its raw coverage cannot pass, so it would need the aligned pair
as the pre-registered statistics. Budget note: the whole 64² screen costs ~30 s of GPU per family at
128 + 32 trajectories, so further variants (longer $T$ for a full domain crossing, $\sigma = 0.05$ at
$128^2$) are cheap if wanted; they were not run here because the three-run budget is used.

## Glossary

- **POD-K floor** — the error left when a held-out vorticity field is projected onto the best
  $K$-dimensional linear subspace of the training fields; the best any linear ROM with $K$ unknowns
  can do. "All" = median over every held-out state; "worst-evolved" = the worst time of each case,
  then the median across cases.
- **Coverage (same-time)** — how far (relative to the field's initial norm) a held-out state is from
  the closest training state at the same output time; small means the training set contains something
  close to every test flow.
- **Aligned** — fields shifted on the torus so that two low Fourier phases are zero; removes the
  translation part of the variation before computing the statistics.
- **Own-norm** — the same error divided by the norm of the state at that time rather than at $t=0$.
- **Held-out / training** — the 32 trajectories used only for scoring / the 128 used to build the
  POD basis and the neighbour set.
- **Newton it/step** — the average number of nonlinear iterations the implicit time stepper needs per
  step; more would mean a more expensive full-order model.
- **CFL** — $\max|u|\,dt/h$; a stability/accuracy indicator of the time step (implicit midpoint is
  stable regardless, but accuracy degrades above ~1).
- **E(T)/E(0), Z(T)/Z(0)** — kinetic energy and enstrophy at the end of the horizon over their initial
  values; how much the flow has decayed.
- **Family / params (P)** — the random-parameter family of initial conditions (and forcing) and its
  number of independent parameters; fewer parameters at a fixed sample count means denser coverage.
- **H-ORACLE, E2** — the plan's pass criterion (best-fit decoder error ≤ ½ the POD-16 error) and the
  next experiment (a shifted-manifold decoder trained on the family chosen here).
